Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining, um we're really excited to scope this pilot with Elysian. quick roll call?
[00:10] Priya: hi yes Priya here, hello.
[00:12] Daniel: Daniel on the line.
[00:14] Sophie: Sophie, compliance.
[00:18] Lucas: Lucas from Redwood, se, thanks.
[00:22] Maya: awesome. goal for today is define success criteria, the bench workload, and a concrete quality eval plan — golden prompts, regression, hallucinations and scoring. also timeline, ok?
[00:35] Priya: sounds good, um high level our product surfaces a multi-field summarization, entity extraction and a short Q&A follow-up. critical is low hallucination on PII and consistent format for downstream parsers.
[00:50] Daniel: to add, traffic shape is spiky - nightly batch of 20k docs and real-time UI at about 25 rps peak, generally 5-8 concurrent long-running sessions. average token length around 600 tokens but summaries usually 150 tokens.
[01:12] Lucas: ok that's helpful. for benching we need: sample of 1k documents representative, golden outputs for 300 examples, and a request histogram (seq length distribution, concurrency). caching is relevant — you said lots of repeated prefixes?
[01:30] Priya: yeah we have templated transcripts so there will be prefix repetition, KV cache could help.
[01:35] Maya: quick question on success criteria — what are the hard gates? e.g., hallucination rate < 2% on golden set? or F1 > 0.85 on entity extraction?
[01:47] Priya: we'd like hallucination below 1.5% for PII fields, overall summary coherence >= 0.8 by human raters, and entity F1 > 0.9 for core fields. those are stretch but important for compliance.
[02:05] Sophie: compliance side: any PII leakage is non-starter. we need audit logs, KMS support, and data residency notes. also SOC2 + ISO documents.
[02:18] Maya: we'll attach our security packet (SOC2, ISO statements) and detail KMS options for both Private and Dedicated.
[02:26] Daniel: timeline wise we have a product deadline in mid-Sep, so pilot needs to wrap and evaluation complete by early Sep to allow integration.
[02:35] Maya: that gives us ~6 weeks; our suggested pilot is 5 weeks with a 2-week benching/ingest window. propose: week 0: kick, infra choose, data transfer; week1: ingest + golden prompt annotation; week2: bench runs + tuning; week3: regression suite & hallucination checks; week4: acceptance + handoff.
[02:58] Priya: ok let's hear details on the quality eval plan — how you structure golden prompts and regressions.
[03:05] Lucas: sure. our typical approach: create a golden prompt set (200-500 items) covering edge cases, hallucination-sensitive examples, and format-critical outputs. we run a deterministic scoring pipeline: exact-match for structured fields, F1 for entities, semantic similarity + human spot checks for free text summaries. we also run synthetic perturbations to catch brittleness.
[03:30] Daniel: what do you mean by synthetic perturbations?
[03:33] Lucas: small typos, redacted PII, shuffled sentence order — if model hallucinate more with small perturbations it's a brittle pattern. we flag those as regression tests.
[03:42] Priya: how do you measure hallucination? it's fuzzy.
[03:45] Lucas: two levels: automatic heuristics and human adjudication. heuristics include entity-overlap checks, hallucination detectors (aux models), and format-conformance checks — for example, if a date field is expected in YYYY-MM-DD and model returns text, that fails format check. heuristics catch ~80%, then we sample a stratified set for human review to estimate true hallucination rate.
[04:10] Maya: we also track a hallucination-rate metric per prompt bucket and per model variant; regressions are defined as >0.5% absolute increase in hallucination or >3% drop in entity F1 over golden baseline.
[04:24] Priya: that threshold seems reasonable, although for PII we may require stricter 0.2% bump threshold.
[04:30] Sophie: yes PII stricter. also we need an audit trail for any human corrections.
[04:36] Lucas: audit trail is standard — all evals produce immutable artifacts and diffs, timestamps, who reviewed. we can integrate with your internal ticketing for reviewer notes.
[04:46] Daniel: latency targets? we need P95 under 700ms for the UI flows, and batch scoring can be higher (2-4s).
[04:55] Maya: on hosted our typical P95 for 150 token responses is ~150-250ms; for 600 tokens P95 can be 450-650ms depending on model. Dedicated can tighten that by ~20-35% with optimized kernels and batch tuning. we will show numbers in bench spreadsheet.
[05:14] Priya: cost is a factor — we may choose quantized model variants if quality delta is acceptable.
[05:20] Lucas: yes Redwood Optimize suggestions will recommend quantization and batching config per workload. we'll propose a primary model (open checkpoint) and a fallback cheaper variant; routing policy keeps quality expectations.
[05:33] Priya: what about KV cache - you mentioned prefix caching earlier. how much does that reduce cost?
[05:37] Lucas: for templated prefixes we typically see 30-60% token-level cost reduction after prefix caching; throughput improves because KV hits reduce attention compute. we'll instrument that in bench runs.
[05:50] Maya: for success criteria let's record concrete gates here:
- Hallucination: <1.5% overall; <0.5% for PII fields (Elysian stricter)
- Entity F1: >=0.9 for core fields
- Summary quality: human-rated coherence >=0.8 average
- P95 latency: <=700ms for UI flows; batch <=4s
- Regression tolerance: no bump >0.5% hallucination or >3% F1 drop (0.2% for PII)
[06:24] Daniel: agreed. what about runbook and bench config?
[06:28] Lucas: runbook includes: data ingest scripts, bench harness (we use a JMeter-like runner + model runner), golden prompt manifest, scoring scripts (exact match, F1, simscore), and hallucination detector config. we'll share the repo link.
[06:42] Priya: can we see the scoring rubric? we need clear thresholds for pass/fail and tie-breakers.
[06:47] Maya: yes rubric: each golden test has primary metric (exact match or F1), a secondary metric (semantic sim or token overlap), and a human-pass flag. Overall pass rate = weighted composite: 50% primary metrics, 30% secondary, 20% human sample. these weights can be adjusted but we want a repeatable number.
[07:10] Priya: human sample size?
[07:12] Lucas: default 200 random stratified samples across buckets, increase if variance high. for critical PII bucket we sample 100% of failing cases.
[07:21] Sophie: for compliance we want to store raw transcripts and eval artifacts for 12 months. retention policy?
[07:26] Maya: we can support 12 months in our dedicated offering, hosted can offer custom retention as add-on. will document retention and export paths.
[07:36] Daniel: what infra options are we choosing for pilot?
[07:39] Priya: we prefer a dedicated pool to mirror production; VPC is required for security but might add lead time.
[07:46] Lucas: Dedicated + VPC is doable; lead time usually 5 business days for provisioning in our standard regions. private/on-prem will be longer.
[07:54] Omar: we may need HSM/KMS integration for keys.
[07:57] Maya: we support both customer-managed KMS and cloud KMS; HSM details on request.
[08:03] Priya: fine. OK benchmarks — what exact workloads will you run?
[08:07] Lucas: three workloads: 1) Real-time UI: 1-50 token prompts, 25 rps spike, target P95 <=700ms; 2) Summarization: 600 token input -> 150 token output, 5 rps sustained, target P95 <=1s on dedicated; 3) Batch nightly: 20k docs, throughput measured in docs/sec and cost per doc, with correctness gates. For each we'll vary concurrency, batch sizes, and enable/disable KV cache.
[08:38] Priya: and golden prompts cover edge-cases?
[08:40] Lucas: yes categories: PII edge-cases, long-context cross-sentence dependencies, format-strict outputs (CSV/JSON), and adversarial paraphrases.
[08:50] Maya: regression cadence — we'll run nightly regression after bench tuning and before acceptance. if a new model is pushed we run full regression.
[08:58] Priya: how do you store regression history?
[09:00] Lucas: we commit baselines to the eval repo with timestamps; diffs stored as artifacts; trend dashboards show F1/hallucination over time.
[09:08] Daniel: ok, let's lock timeline. earlier you proposed 5 weeks. can you lay out milestones and deliverables?
[09:14] Maya: yes milestone list:
- Week 0 (kick): infra selection, NDAs/ops access, S3 transfer method decided
- Week 1: data ingest + annotate golden set (Priya owns prompts)
- Week 2: initial bench runs, latency & cost baseline (Redwood runs)
- Week 3: tuning (quantization / batching), rerun bench, run hallucination detectors
- Week 4: regression runs, human sampling, final acceptance report
- Week 5 (buffer): integration support + knowledge transfer
[10:00] Priya: that maps well — we need acceptance report by 2027-08-31 to meet mid-Sept launch, so this fits.
[10:08] Sophie: compliance docs needed by 2027-07-24 so legal can review.
[10:13] Maya: noted.
[10:15] Priya: a few nitty bits — scoring approach for free-text summaries, semantic sim thresholds?
[10:20] Lucas: we use a dual metric: normalized BLEU/ROUGE variants for surface overlap plus embedding-based cosine similarity with a threshold (>=0.72 for pass). human sample will validate borderline cases.
[10:33] Priya: ok makes sense. also logging — do you capture token-level cost metrics?
[10:38] Maya: yes console shows per-request token breakdown, per-route cost, and token-level latency distributions. we'll show a sample dashboard.
[10:46] Daniel: what about retraining? if we find systematic errors, how do we loop feedback?
[10:50] Lucas: typical path: capture failing prompts into a golden-regression set, label them, and either fine-tune or use prompt engineering + reranker. we can help with recommendations; retrain is customer's choice.
[11:03] Priya: ok last question — do you support staged rollouts to production?
[11:06] Maya: yes canary and A/B rollouts with automatic fallback to previous model variant if regressions detected. we can wire this into your CI.
[11:14] Priya: great.
[11:16] Maya: quick recap and next steps: 1) Redwood to send pilot runbook + bench template (Maya) by 7/23; 2) Elysian to provide golden prompts (Priya) + sample logs by 7/25; 3) Redwood+Elysian to schedule bench run 7/28; 4) Sophie to list compliance docs by 7/24.
[11:36] Daniel: sounds good.
[11:38] Sophie: thanks everyone.
[11:40] Maya: thanks, we'll follow up by email and attach links to the runbook + security packet.
[11:45] (call end)
